artists.biography:
The Coral are an English band formed  in 1996 in Hoylake on the Wirral Peninsula in England. The band first emerged during the early 2000s (decade)  and found success with their debut album The Coral (2002) and follow up Magic and Medicine (2003). Their self-titled debut album was nominated for the 2002 Mercury Music Prize  and later voted the fourth best album of the year by NME Magazine.

The band continued to record and tour throughout the decade releasing the albums The Invisible Invasion (2005) and Roots & Echoes (2007).

In 2008 guitarist Bill Ryder-Jones left the band, however The Coral continued as a five-piece. Their sixth album Butterfly House was released in 2010.

perplexity.description:
Sea of Mirrors is the eleventh studio album by English rock band The Coral, released on September 8, 2023, through Modern Sky UK and Run On Records. The album is a stylistic departure from their previous work, drawing inspiration from the cinematic soundscapes of Spaghetti Westerns, particularly the music of Ennio Morricone. Produced by Sean O'Hagan, the record blends alternative and indie rock with neo-psychedelic and British trad rock elements, creating a lush, atmospheric sound. Guest appearances include former member Bill Ryder-Jones, actor Cillian Murphy, and Love guitarist Johnny Echols, adding further depth and texture to the album’s sonic palette.

Musically, Sea of Mirrors is concise and evocative, clocking in at just over 36 minutes. It follows the widely acclaimed 2021 double album Coral Island, but instead of expanding on that project’s narrative, The Coral offer a more abstract, soundtrack-like experience. The album’s singles—“Wild Bird,” “Oceans Apart,” and “That’s Where She Belongs”—highlight its blend of cinematic ambition, melodic richness, and subtle psych-pop flourishes. Critics have noted the album’s imaginative concept and strong songwriting, positioning it as a distinctive and adventurous entry in The Coral’s discography.
